keepCall: The invocation itself is needed to continue the latest user task correctly. Retain unique unresolved actions, edits, decisions, or essential provenance. Completed setup, repeated exploration, superseded checks, and commands whose conclusions are already stated in preserved assistant/user text are not needed. Reads of the active task contract or governing instructions are essential provenance until that task finishes, even when the read succeeded. For other calls, retaining the invocation and a short result prefix is sufficient when only proof of an action or check remains useful.
keepResult: The exact result body is needed verbatim to continue the latest user task correctly. Retain unique actionable diagnostics, exact interfaces, or data not recoverable from preserved user/assistant text. Routine success output, already summarized evidence, duplicated file dumps, and completed-work logs do not require verbatim preservation. Exception: retain the exact active task contract and governing instructions, including canonical instruction paths, authorization boundaries, verification requirements, and reporting commands. Their read completing and an assistant paraphrasing them do not make them disposable. For other output, judge the need for the full body separately from the importance of knowing the call occurred: a preserved invocation and 300-character prefix suffice for routine action and check provenance.
